assays.assay_description: 41 × 20 × 24 cm open-field arena, ~200-250 lux; mice placed individually in a corner and allowed to explore freely for 10 min (acute, at 15 min and 4 h post-injection) or 150 min (at 7 days). Total distance traveled and time in center (middle one-third, 6 × 27 cm) measured by Any-Maze.

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin produced bidirectional, dose-dependent effects on time in center: significant suppression at 15 min (acute anxiogenic-like) and significant enhancement at 4 h (postacute anxiolytic-like) with 3 mg/kg. At 7 days, psilocybin increased time in center during a 150 min OFT, but this long-term anxiolytic effect was abolished by chronic oral corticosterone exposure. Distance traveled was not significantly altered.
outcomes.statistics: Time in center: two-way RM ANOVA dose × time interaction p = 0.0019, Sidak's *p = 0.047, **p = 0.001. Distance: dose × time interaction p = 0.034. 7-day OFT: psilocybin × corticosterone interaction p = 0.0115, drug main effect p < 0.0001, Sidak's vs saline *p = 0.046.
outcomes.evidence: A negative relationship between the dose and the time spent in the center of the open field was seen at 15 min ... In contrast, a positive relationship between the dose and the time spent in the center of the open field was observed at 4 h.

assays.assay_description: Mice implanted with skull-mounted neodymium magnets were placed individually in a clear acrylic cylinder (15.24 × 15.24 cm) wrapped in copper coil within a dark sound-attenuating chamber. Following 3 mg/kg IP psilocybin, magnetometer signals were recorded for 2 h and head twitches automatically detected via custom MATLAB software in 10 min bins.

setup_restrain.evidence: individual animals were placed into a clear acrylic cylinder

food_restriction.evidence: No food in HTR cylinder during recording.

water_restriction.evidence: No water in HTR cylinder during recording.

time_to_assay.evidence: the animals were administered with 3 mg/kg IP psilocybin and recorded for an additional 2 h

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin (3 mg/kg IP) produced a robust elevation in head twitch counts during the first 10 min post-injection that rapidly returned to baseline.
outcomes.statistics: Two-way RM ANOVA (n = 7-8; drug × time interaction p < 0.0001; drug main effect p < 0.0001; time main effect p = 0.48) with Sidak's *p = 0.031.
outcomes.evidence: Psilocybin-treated animals demonstrated a clear elevation in the number of HTRs occurring in the first 10 min after IP administration, which rapidly returned to baseline

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Head twitch counts across 10 min bins following psilocybin administration

B4_ethological.evidence: Per rubric, HTR is explicitly NOT ethological.

B5_social.evidence: individual animals were placed into a clear acrylic cylinder

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Magnetometer signal processing with custom MATLAB; not a video-based behavioural classifier on rubric's allow-list.

E1_environment_type.evidence: clear acrylic cylinder (15.24 cm height × 15.24 cm diameter)

assays.assay_description: After 16 h food deprivation, mice received saline or drug IP 4 h prior to testing. They were placed in a novel cage (60 × 40 × 40 cm, 960 lux) with a sucrose-soaked food pellet on a petri dish in the center and observed for 10 min. Latency to first feed (blinded scoring), movement/distance (Any-Maze), time in center, and pellet weight change were measured.

application_type.evidence: Mice then received an IP injection of saline or drug 4 h prior to performing the NSF test

setup_restrain.evidence: placed into a corner of the apparatus and allowed to explore for 10 min

food_restriction.evidence: Animals underwent a 16 h period of food deprivation

time_to_assay.evidence: IP injection of saline or drug 4 h prior to performing the NSF test

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin (3 mg/kg IP) reduced latency to first feed and increased time in the center of the NSF chamber 4 h post-injection, indicating anxiolytic-like effects. This effect was blocked by 21-day chronic oral corticosterone, by mifepristone pretreatment, and by withdrawal from prior chronic corticosterone, but NOT by ketanserin (5-HT2A antagonist). Lisuride and repeated saline injection produced similar latency reductions, supporting a glucocorticoid-mediated mechanism.
outcomes.statistics: Mantel-Cox (n = 30; ***p = 0.001); time in center t-test **p = 0.0047; mifepristone block Mantel-Cox p = 0.0003 (Psil vs saline **p = 0.0075; Psil vs Psil+Mifep *p = 0.0174); ketanserin no block (Psil vs Psil+Ketans p = 0.45); chronic CORT block p = 0.16; withdrawal block p = 0.59.
outcomes.evidence: psilocybin was found to reduce the latency to first consumption in the NSF assay ... Animals treated with 3 mg/kg IP psilocybin also exhibited increased time in the center of this assay at 4 h posttreatment

B1_num_measures.evidence: Latency to first feed, time in center, distance/movement (Any-Maze), and pellet weight change before/after test

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Single latency / aggregate measures over 10 min.

B4_ethological.evidence: Feeding behaviour (latency to feed, pellet consumption) is a natural behavior directly measured.

B6_cognitive.evidence: Approach-avoidance conflict; no learned association required.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Any-Maze tracking only; latency scored by blinded observer.

E6_spatial.evidence: Single arena with central petri dish.

E8_food_water.evidence: A food pellet soaked in 50% sucrose solution was placed into a glass petri dish that served as the center zone

D3_recording_days.evidence: Single test day at 4 h post-injection.

judge_notes: Three behavioural assays retained (OFT, HTR, NSF). All non-behavioural endpoints (plasma corticosterone ELISA, LC-MS/MS pharmacokinetics) excluded per rubric.

FST and SPT mentioned in main text as supplementary (Figure S2) — not scored as separate assays because supplement details unavailable in the provided markdown and main text only briefly references null results.
B4 (ethological) for NSF scored Yes because feeding is a natural behaviour directly measured (latency to first feed, pellet consumption); candidates disagreed and this matches gptoss reading.
B1 for NSF set to 2-3+ → '4-6' (score 2): latency, time in center, distance/movement, and pellet weight change = 4 distinct measures.
Dosing block expanded to include Ketamine and Lisuride, which were also administered to mice in behavioural experiments (NSF), in addition to Psilocybin.
B7 scored 0 for all assays: Any-Maze is position tracking (rubric SCORE 0 list); HTR magnetometer signal processing is not on the SCORE 1 allow-list.
Handling scored not_reported (low confidence) — paper mentions 'prior to handling or experimentation' as acclimation context but does not describe a habituation handling protocol.
